t.7.52.1: Then Sumantra approached Rāghava and spoke these words: "O king, these ascetics stand at the gate, held back."
t.7.52.2: O great king, the great sages who dwell on the banks of the Yamunā, placing at their head the Bhārgava named Cyavana, are urging in haste for an audience with you, O tiger among men, and they are well pleased.
t.7.52.3: Having heard those words of his, Rāma, the knower of dharma, said: "Let the great-souled twice-born, headed by Bhārgava, be shown in."
t.7.52.4: Then the doorkeeper, honoring the king's command, with joined palms raised to his head, ushered in the many esteemed ascetics.
t.7.52.5: There, more than a hundred great-souled ascetics, blazing with their own splendour, entered the royal palace.
t.7.52.7: Rāma, filled with delight, accepted all of that, the waters of all the sacred fords and fruits of many kinds.
t.7.52.6: Those twice-born, bearing brimming pitchers, took up fruits and roots honoured with the waters of all the sacred fords, and brought them in abundance to Rāma.
t.7.52.8: And the mighty-armed one said to all the great sages: "Here are these excellent seats; let them be taken, each according to his due."
t.7.52.9: Having heard Rāma's words, all those great sages sat down on splendid golden seats.
t.7.52.10: Seeing the sages seated there, Rāghava, conqueror of enemy cities, became composed and, with joined palms, spoke these words.
t.7.52.11: What is the purpose of your coming? What shall I do, O ascetics rich in penance? I am to be commanded by the great sages, and I will gladly fulfil all your wishes.
t.7.52.12: This entire kingdom, and the life that dwells in my heart, all of this of mine is for the sake of the twice-born; this truth I declare to you.
t.7.52.13: Having heard those words of his, a great cry of approval arose from the sages of fierce austerities who dwelt on the banks of the Yamunā.
t.7.52.14: And those great-souled ones, filled with great joy, said: “O best of men, this befits you alone on earth, and no one else.”
t.7.52.15: Many mighty kings of the earth, O king, have passed away who, not heeding the gravity of the duty, did not see fit to honour their pledge.
t.7.52.16: This promise was made by you out of reverence for the brāhmaṇas, without even considering the reason; now fulfil it, for you are surely the one who acts, there is no doubt of that. You ought to save the sages from this great fear.
